03/27.07.2017 No one appears on behalf of the petitioner.
However, Mr. Md. Asif Khan, learned A.P.P., is present.
As the matter is pending since the year 2005 the same is being disposed of based on the material available on record.

This application is directed against the judgment dated 14.12.2004 passed in Criminal Appeal No. 91 of 2003 by the learned Additional Judicial Commissioner, Fast Track Court, Khunti, Ranchi whereby and whereunder the judgment and order of conviction and sentence passed by the learned Sub Divisional Judicial Magistrate, Khunti, Ranchi in Case No. 22 II-B/98 by which the petitioner has been convicted for the offence punishable under Section 16(1)
(a)(b) of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act, 1954 and sentenced to undergo simple imprisonment for a period of six months as also a fine of Rs. 1,000/- has been affirmed.

sentences.text: The prosecution story as would appear from the prosecution report is that 600 grams of Rahar Dal was taken from the shop of the petitioner on 29.10.1996 and the receipt was also granted in favour of the petitioner.
The seized Rahar Dal was sealed in three packets each containing 200 grams and was sent to the public analyst for analysis.

The report opined that sample of Rahar Dal contained coal tar (metanil yellow) and since the same was found to be adulterated, the prosecution report was filed under Section 16(1)(a)(b) of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act against the petitioner which was registered as Case No. 22 II-B/98.
In course of trial the prosecution had examined as many as three witnesses in support of its case.

1 P.W. - 1, Mahendra Nath Sahu, is the Food Inspector who had stated that he had gone to the shop of the petitioner on 29.10.1996 along with one Siban Hazam and Vishwanath Singh Munda.

sentences.text: He had stated that 600 grams of Rahar Dal was taken as sample which were kept in three packets containing 200 grams each and a receipt was also given to the petitioner.
He had further stated that he had dispatched one sample to the public analyst through memorandum which was marked as Exhibit - 2.

He had further stated that after obtaining the report of the public analyst he wrote a letter to the Civil surgeon, Ranchi for sanctioning of the prosecution and after obtaining the sanction the complaint was filed.
P.W. - 2, Vishwanath Singh Munda, had stated that he was present when the sample of Rahar Dal was taken from the shop of the petitioner.

P.W. - 3, Siban Hazam, had also supported the version of P.W. - 1 and P.W. - 2 and had stated that he was also present when the sample was taken and the receipt was granted in favour of the petitioner.

Since the prosecution had been able to prove its case beyond all reasonable doubt the petitioner was convicted by the learned Sub-Divisional Judicial Magistrate, Khunti Ranchi in Case No. 22 II-B/98 on 04.08.2003 for the offence under Section 16(1)(a)(b) of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act and was sentenced to undergo simple imprisonment for six months along with a fine of Rs. 1,000/-.
The petitioner preferred an appeal being Criminal Appeal No. 91 of 2003 which however was dismissed by the learned Additional Judicial Commissioner, Fast Track Court, Khunti, Ranchi on 14.12.2004.
The main plank of argument before the learned trial court on behalf of the petitioner was that proper compliance was not made with respect to Section 13(2) of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act.
The learned courts below have taken into consideration the plea raised by the petitioner but has not appreciated the legal points involved in the said plea.
Section 13 of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act, 1954 deals with the report of public analyst and sub-section (2) of Section 13 reads as follows:-

" (2) On receipt of the report of the result of the analysis under sub-section (1) to the effect that the article of food is adulterated, the Local (Health) Authority shall, after the institution of prosecution against the persons from whom the sample of the article of food was taken and the person, if any, whose name, address and other particulars have been disclosed under section 14A, forward, in such manner as may be prescribed, a copy of the report of the result of the analysis to such person or persons, as the case may be, informing such person or persons that if it is so desired,
either or both of them may make an application to the court within a period of ten days from the date of receipt of the copy of the report to get the sample of the article of food kept by the Local (Health) Authority analysed by the Central Food Laboratory."

2 Sub-section (2) of Section 13, therefore, clearly reveals that as soon as the report of the public analyst is made available a copy of the same has to be given to the person/persons who are aggrieved by the report of the public analyst so that they can make an application to the concerned court within a period of ten days from the date of receipt of a copy of the report to get the sample of the article of food analyzed by the Central Food Laboratory.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The word used in sub-section (2) of Section 13 would indicate that it is mandatory provision which has to be followed by the authority and the person/persons who are aggrieved has to be given a copy of the public analyst report so that they may avail the remedy if they so choose to get the sample analyzed by the Central Food Laboratory if an application is filed and allowed by the concerned court.
In the backdrop of the provisions of Section 13(2) of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act the report of the public analyst has to be considered.
The said report has been marked as Exhibit - 4 by the prosecution.
The report merely contains that the sample of Rahar Dal was adulterated as it included coal tar (metanil yellow).

The report of the public analyst, no where disclosed that the petitioner was duly informed of his rights to make an application before the concerned court for getting the said sample tested by the Central Food Laboratory.
Non -compliance of the Section 13(2) of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act had virtually extinguished the right of the petitioner to challenge the report of the public analyst.

The learned courts below have merely considered the fact that no application has been filed by the petitioner before the learned court below for getting the sample tested without looking into the report of the public analyst.

Even if the report of the public analyst is served upon the petitioner that also would not be in actual compliance for the provisions of Section 13(2) of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act as it was incumbent upon the authorities to inform the petitioner of his right if he wants to get the sample tested by the Central Food Laboratory.
Such circumstance having not been properly appreciated either by the learned trial court or by the learned appellate court the benefit of doubt has to go to the petitioner.

Accordingly, in view of what has been discussed above, this application is allowed and the judgment dated dated 14.12.2004 passed in Criminal Appeal No. 91 of 2003 by the learned Additional Judicial Commissioner, Fast Track Court, Khunti, Ranchi and the judgment and order of conviction and sentence passed by the learned Sub Divisional Judicial Magistrate, Khunti, Ranchi in Case No. 22 II-B/98 are, hereby, set aside.
The petitioner is discharged from the liability of his bail bond.
(Rongon Mukhopadhyay, J.) Umesh/-
